20	`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is

25	CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
26	repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
27	`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
28	worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it

30	`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by

34	`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
35	paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

content.text: This is the known Apple `ar` 4 GiB archive-size limit hitting `liblibslic3r_gui.a` — I have a memory of this exact failure with a documented fix. Let me pull it up.

3	description: "RelWithDebInfo liblibslic3r_gui.a crossed Apple ar's 4 GiB archive limit on jusprin-newui (2026-09-13); CMAKE_AR override is ignored; manual llvm-ar relink recipe and its cd trap"
4	metadata:

10	
11	On 2026-09-13, at jusprin-newui 770bd2b0a2 (after "Add the evidence-led Add a
12	printer flow"), a worktree RelWithDebInfo build failed archiving
13	`src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a`:
14	`Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF) ... ArchiveWriter.cpp` then
15	`fatal error in .../ranlib`. The archive llvm-ar produced was 4,309,350,176
16	bytes; the main checkout's copy built minutes earlier was 4,143,827,796 and
17	still fit. Objects are big because the root CMakeLists.txt (lines ~544-548)
18	rewrites RelWithDebInfo -O2 to -O0 on purpose. Disk space was not the cause.
19	
20	**Why:** the failed build left the OLD harness binary in place, and the harness
21	runs afterwards "passed" against stale code (a new `--printer-setup` flag
22	silently ran the default mode: same 285 check count). Gate runs on build
23	success and compare binary mtime.
24	
25	**How to apply:**
26	- `-DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` on an existing build dir does
27	  nothing: `CMakeFiles/<ver>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` sets CMAKE_AR as a normal
28	  variable that shadows the cache.
29	- Working relink: `ninja -f build-RelWithDebInfo.ninja -t commands <target>`,
30	  drop compile lines, swap ar/ranlib for llvm-ar/llvm-ranlib on the gui archive
31	  line only, then run EACH line in its own `(cd build/arm64 && eval "$line")`.
32	  One `sh` script fails with bogus "no such file" errors because the
33	  encoding-check line does `cd src/slic3r` and it leaks; `sh -e` also does not
34	  stop inside `&&` chains. Apple's linker accepted the >4 GiB llvm-ar archive.
35	- A lasting fix (llvm-ar in the toolchain, thin archives, or less debug info)
36	  is Kenneth's call; the main checkout will hit this on its next growth.
37	
38	Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

# macOS build troubleshooting

Recipes for build failures on this fork that are environment/toolchain issues,
not code regressions. Kept separate from `agent-docs/jusprin/` because these
apply to the OrcaSlicer build system generally, not to JusPrin product code.

## `liblibslic3r_gui.a` exceeds 4 GiB: Apple `ar`/`ranlib` assertion

### Symptom

`./build_release_macos.sh -s -x -b -c RelWithDebInfo` (or any RelWithDebInfo
build of the `slicer` target) fails while archiving, not compiling:

```
[36/42] Linking CXX static library src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a
FAILED: [code=1] src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a
Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF), function update_block_invoke, file ArchiveWriter.cpp, line 276.
fatal error: .../usr/bin/ar: fatal error in .../usr/bin/ranlib
```

All `.cpp`/`.mm` files for `libslic3r_gui` compiled fine; only the final
archive step fails.

### Root cause

Apple's stock `ar`/`ranlib` (from the Xcode toolchain) use 32-bit member
offsets internally and assert once an archive crosses 4 GiB
(`0xFFFFFFFF` bytes). `liblibslic3r_gui.a` in `RelWithDebInfo` carries full
debug info at `-O0` — the root `CMakeLists.txt` (around line 544-548)
deliberately rewrites `RelWithDebInfo` from `-O2` to `-O0` for easier
debugging — and as the JusPrin fork has added more GUI code (`Agent/`,
`PrinterSetup/`, `Home/`, `Mcp/`, `Shell/`, `Workspace/`, etc.), the archive
has grown past that limit. This first hit on `jusprin-newui` on 2026-09-13 at
commit `770bd2b0a2`; it will recur, and get worse, as the fork keeps growing.
It is not disk space (plenty was free) and not a code bug — the same source
links fine once a 64-bit-capable archiver is used.

### Fix: use LLVM's `ar`/`ranlib` instead of Apple's

LLVM's archiver (installed via `brew install llvm`, present at
`/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` and `llvm-ranlib`) has no such limit and
accepted a 4,288,175,376-byte archive without complaint.

**The trap:** `-DCMAKE_AR=...` on an *existing* build directory does nothing.
CMake only auto-detects the archiver once, the first time it determines the
C/C++ compiler, and bakes the result into
`build/arm64/CMakeFiles/<cmake-version>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` (and the `C`
equivalent) as a literal `set(CMAKE_AR "...")`. That generated file also sets
`CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID_RUN 1`, and every later `cmake ..` reconfigure loads it
first and skips compiler/archiver detection entirely because that variable is
already set — so a `-DCMAKE_AR=` flag on a reconfigure is silently ignored.
(Verified 2026-09-13 by reading CMake 3.29's own
`CMakeDetermineCXXCompiler.cmake` and `CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake.in`.)

To make the override take effect, CMake has to redo compiler detection from
scratch. Two ways to get there:

**Option A — targeted reset (cheaper, not yet verified end-to-end).** Delete
just the compiler-detection cache files, then reconfigure:

```bash
rm -rf build/arm64/CMakeFiles/3.29.0/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake \
       build/arm64/CMakeFiles/3.29.0/CMakeCCompiler.cmake \
       build/arm64/CMakeFiles/3.29.0/CMakeDetermineCompilerABI_CXX.bin \
       build/arm64/CMakeFiles/3.29.0/CMakeDetermineCompilerABI_C.bin \
       build/arm64/CMakeFiles/3.29.0/CompilerIdC \
       build/arm64/CMakeFiles/3.29.0/CompilerIdCXX
cd build/arm64
cmake . -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

`ar`/`ranlib` only matter for the final archive step, not for compiling each
`.cpp`, so this is expected to make Ninja only relink static-library targets
rather than recompile every translation unit — but this has not been proven
in practice. Adjust `3.29.0` to match your CMake version
(`build/arm64/CMakeFiles/` has the exact directory name).

**Option B — full clean reconfigure (guaranteed, expensive; this is what was
actually run and verified on 2026-09-13).** Wipe the whole build directory —
it is pure generated output, safe to delete — and reconfigure from nothing:

```bash
rm -rf build/arm64
mkdir -p build/arm64
cd build/arm64
cmake /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin \
  -G "Ninja Multi-Config" \
  -DORCA_TOOLS=ON \
  REDACTED \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=11.3 \
  -DCMAKE_IGNORE_PREFIX_PATH="/opt/local:/usr/local:/opt/homebrew" \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar \
  -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local"
cmake --build . --config RelWithDebInfo --target all
```

This pays for a full rebuild of the entire slicer target (every `.cpp`/`.mm`
file, not just `libslic3r_gui`) at `-O0` with full debug info, so budget real
time for it (order of an hour on Apple Silicon).

**Deps-path gotcha, easy to miss:** on this machine, `JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local`
is an empty skeleton — no Boost, no TBB, nothing — kept that way to save
disk. The real, already-built dependencies for this fork
(Boost 1.84.0, TBB, OpenSSL, CURL, Freetype, libpng, NLopt, OpenVDB, GMP/MPFR,
OpenCV, JPEG, wxWidgets, etc.) live in the sibling checkout at
`~/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local`. A fresh
configure that only uses `build_release_macos.sh`'s own computed
`CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` (JusPrin's own deps dir) fails immediately with `Could
NOT find Boost`. Always include the OrcaSlicer sibling path too, as shown
above — this mirrors the worktree build pattern already used for
`jusprin-newui` worktrees.

### Once fixed

`build/arm64`'s CMake cache now has `llvm-ar`/`llvm-ranlib` and the correct
`CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` baked in, so ordinary incremental builds — including

1	# Fake Bambu printer (in-process)
2	
3	Substitutes `FakeBambuAgent` for Bambu's closed network plugin so header menu,
4	Select Machine, and print can run without hardware. It is not a network fake:
5	MQTT, FTPS, and discovery are not implemented.
6	
7	The Klipper/Moonraker simulator lives on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` under
8	`tests/printer_sim/` and covers print-host printers. Do not add a Bambu network
9	fake unless asked.
10	
11	This file is the operator guide for humans and AI agents.
12	
13	## What success looks like
14	
15	- Log: `switch_printer_agent: printer agent switched to jusprin-fake-bambu`
16	- Log: `set_selected_machine=FAKE001` and later `FakeBambuAgent: connected FAKE001`
17	- Printer chip shows `Bambu Lab A1 mini · 0.4` (nickname and nozzle only)
18	- Click the **printer** half of that chip. The **first menu row** is Idle,
19	  Printing, or Offline. Those words are never on the chip itself.
20	
21	If the log says `moonraker` or `orca`, the fake is not in the path. Stop and
22	fix the preset; do not patch UI gates.
23	
24	## Turn it on
25	
26	Quit JusPrin first. The app rewrites `JusPrin2.conf` on exit.
27	
28	`JusPrin2.conf` is JSON. Under the scratch datadir:
29	
30	```json
31	"jusprin": { "fake_printer": true }
32	```
33	
34	JSON `true` is what the app stores; `get("jusprin", "fake_printer")` reads as
35	the string `"true"`. An INI `[jusprin]` block is ignored.
36	
37	Keep a **real Bambu Lab system preset** selected, typically
38	`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle`. `is_bbl_vendor()` must be true. An embedded
39	3mf preset named `Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle(Tape_4_3MF.3mf)` is not enough;
40	the agent stays `orca`.
41	
42	Install the system preset with **Add a printer…** in the printer menu, or copy
43	`Resources/profiles/BBL` into `<datadir>/system/` and add the A1 mini model to
44	the `models` array in `JusPrin2.conf`. Opening `~/Downloads/Tape_4_3MF.3mf`
45	only helps after that vendor is installed.
46	
47	Launch a **scratch** `--datadir`. Do not point fake mode at the everyday
48	config. Set `"single_instance": false` in the `app` object if another JusPrin
49	is already running. Do not pass `--no-single-instance`; Boost rejects it.
50	
51	The fake emulates printer type `N1` (A1 mini). Select Machine lists it as
52	**JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)**.
53	
54	## Drive state
55	
56	Write `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (create `jusprin/` if needed). The
57	fake rereads it about once a second.
58	
59	```json
60	{"state":"printing","progress":0.4,"nozzle":210,"bed":60,"offline":false}
61	```
62	
63	| Field | Meaning |
64	|---|---|
65	| `state` | `idle`, `heating`/`prepare`, `printing`/`running`, `pause`, `finished`, `failed` |
66	| `progress` | 0–1, mapped to `mc_percent` |
67	| `nozzle`, `bed` | °C |
68	| `offline` | `true` stops `push_status`; after ~30 s the menu first row is Offline |
69	
70	Delete the file, or set `"offline": false` and `"state":"idle"`, to return to Idle.
71	
72	## Print
73	
74	Slice, then Print (or Cmd+Shift+G on macOS). Send completes without a printer.
75	The log records `FakeBambuAgent: start_local_print file=...`.
76	
77	If the control file is present, that file wins: send still succeeds, but the
78	menu stays on the file's state. Remove the file if you want the canned printing
79	scenario after send.
80	
81	## Isolate a running app (agents)
82	
83	Another JusPrin may already be open. Do not send keys or clicks to it.
84	
85	On macOS both processes are often named `OrcaSlicer`. Target by unix pid or by
86	a unique `CFBundleIdentifier` on a ditto'd `.app` (then ad-hoc `codesign`).
87	`osascript` `unix id` filters can match the wrong process; prefer
88	`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` or the unique bundle id.
89	
90	Keyboard events posted to the pid work while the Mac is locked; mouse events
91	posted that way do not. Menus only open when that app is frontmost. The printer
92	half of the chip is a wx control (`SetName("Printer")`) and often has no AX
93	title; click by coordinates after a screenshot, or use the documented shortcut
94	for Print.
95	
96	Logs: `<datadir>/log/debug_*.log`. This machine's default `grep` may be ugrep;
97	use `/usr/bin/grep -a` on app logs.
98	
99	## Unit tests
100	
101	`jusprin_fake_bambu_tests` (Catch2, GUI build). They cover announce JSON,
102	control-file parsing, and agent id. They do not start the heartbeat unless the
103	test sets `set_queue_on_main_fn`.
104	
105	## Agent id
106	
107	Registered as `jusprin-fake-bambu`. `GUI_App::switch_printer_agent` uses that
108	id in place of `bbl` when fake mode is on. No other upstream file is involved.

## Discrepancies found

I compared the built app's Add Printer flow (built from this worktree, now rebased onto `claude/add-printer-flow-changes-d2e0fa`) against the six Figma frames on the "Add Printer Flow" page (18a–18f) at [the JusPrin v2 Figma file](https://www.figma.com/design/jo9J1sK9ZZ0vxncWnSp0vH/JusPrin-v2?node-id=636-375). I ran the app with a fresh, isolated profile and no AI agent configured, which is the one state reachable without live credentials or network discovery: frame 18f ("No agent connected").

**1. "Set it up myself" opens the wrong screen — confirmed bug.**
In Figma's 18e frame, clicking "Set it up myself" is supposed to open a screen scoped to the flow: a two-panel dialog showing only Bambu Lab printer models, a sidebar for Printer/Filaments/Bed shape/Firmware, and a link back to "Ask the agent instead" — all inside the same "Add a printer" modal. In the running app, that link instead opens OrcaSlicer's original, unrelated setup wizard: a generic grid of every supported vendor (Klipper, Marlin, RepRap, Afinia, and dozens more), with plain Confirm/Create/Cancel buttons and no way back to the agent. This is the same wizard screen that appears on first launch, before any of the new Add Printer flow work. I confirmed this both by reading the source ([PrinterSetupDialog.cpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterSetupDialog.cpp) lines 338 and 401 call Orca's original `ConfigWizard` directly) and by clicking through it live.

**2. The "No agent connected" screen (18f) matches Figma closely.**
Title, body copy, the "Set up the agent" button, the caption underneath, and the "Or set it up myself from the lists" footer link all match the mockup almost exactly in wording, layout, and color. The one difference is expected, not a bug: Figma's mockup shows a printer already found on the network, while the real test machine has none, so the app correctly shows "No supported printers found yet." instead.

**3. "Set up the agent" routes correctly.**
Clicking it leaves the printer dialog and opens the Agent Setup screen, matching the routing note Figma's designer left on the page ("18f 'Set up the agent' → Agent Setup - Empty State page"). Not a bug.

**4. Four states I could not visually check this pass: 18a (Initial), 18b (Recognized), 18c (Network Selected), 18d (Ambiguous).**
These only appear once an AI agent is configured with real credentials, or when a real printer is found on the network — neither is available in this sandboxed test environment, and I didn't want to enter live credentials without asking first. The source code does have these states individually named to match the Figma frame numbers (a good sign the implementation was built frame-by-frame against this same mockup), but I haven't independently confirmed they render correctly. There's already a test harness (`tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp --printer-setup`) built specifically to reach these states deterministically without live credentials — that would be the next step if you want full coverage.

I saved these findings to memory for future reference. Let me know if you'd like me to dig into the four unverified states using that test harness, or file the "Set it up myself" issue as something to fix.

Reparenting a live `wxWebView` isn't something this codebase does today, but there's a working precedent one file over: `WipeTowerDialog` in [WipeTowerDialog.cpp:366-422](src/slic3r/GUI/WipeTowerDialog.cpp:366) already hosts a self-contained `wxWebView` inside a plain modal dialog, sized to the dialog rather than the full window.

The main tradeoff is that it touches more than the printer dialog — you'd be changing `ShellController`'s docking/resize code and the dialog's modal lifecycle (`EndModal`/`ShowModal` timing around the reparent), not just adding a webview to a sizer. Want me to turn this into a concrete implementation plan?
WipeTowerDialog gives a concrete template for the wx side of it - which side is missing an existing example for reparenting?

`WipeTowerDialog` only shows one side: creating a **fresh** `wxWebView` from scratch, owned by and scoped to the dialog for its lifetime, then destroyed when the dialog closes. That's a "new box, new webpage" pattern.

Yes — code-wise, spinning up a second webview is much simpler: no reparenting, no touching `ShellController`'s docking logic, just instantiate a second `AgentWebView` inside the dialog. But here's the concrete, code-confirmed problem with doing that:

**The scenario:**

1. The app is running with the normal docked Agent panel (call it webview A) in its "no agent configured" state.
2. User opens "Add a printer," clicks "Set up the agent," and — in the new embedded webview (call it webview B) — enters an API key under "Use your own API key."
3. B verifies the key and calls `commit()` ([AgentConfiguration.cpp:110-121](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentConfiguration.cpp:110)), which saves the key to the macOS keychain and writes `provider`/`enabled`/`cloud_consent` onto the app's shared config object. That part is fine — it's a single shared config, not two copies.
4. But immediately after that, B flips its *own* internal `m_agent`/`m_availability` to "Ready" ([AgentHost.cpp:1474](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentHost.cpp:1474)). That's a private field on B's `AgentHost` instance — A's `AgentHost` instance is never told the config changed. There's no event, no callback, no file-watcher between the two; I checked and the only place that re-derives availability from config is a one-time call at app startup ([ShellController.cpp:201](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.cpp:201)), never repeated.
5. User closes the printer dialog (destroying B) and reopens "Add a printer." The dialog decides whether to show "No agent connected" by reading availability from **A** specifically ([PrinterSetupLauncher.cpp:86-87](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterSetupLauncher.cpp:86)) — and A is still stuck on "Unavailable," because A never re-read the config B just wrote.

Good news: this is a stronger design than "reload," and it already has a precedent in this exact codebase.

**The event already exists.** `ShellController::on_page_changed()` ([ShellController.cpp:491](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.cpp:491)) fires every time the top-level tab switches between Home and Prepare (bound to `wxEVT_NOTEBOOK_PAGE_CHANGED`). It's coarse-grained — only top-level tab changes, not every camera move or click — and it already does precisely the pattern you're describing, just for a different panel: when Home becomes active, it calls `m_home->refresh()`, with a comment explicitly justifying it: *"The gallery is a view of state that changes while another screen is in front... refreshed on the way in rather than kept live behind the canvas."* That's your exact argument, already applied once.

**One correction to your proposal: don't reload, push.** I checked what `m_home->refresh()` actually does — [HomeWebView.cpp:94](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/HomeWebView.cpp:94): `m_host->push_state()`. That's a targeted bridge message that pushes fresh data into the *already-running* React app, not a full `Reload()`/`LoadURL()` of the webview. That distinction matters: a true reload would blow away any in-progress Agent conversation in the docked panel — unsent draft text, scroll position, open thread. A `push_state()`-style refresh doesn't, because the page never re-navigates. So the design should be: on `on_page_changed()`, have webview A re-derive its availability from `AppConfig` (the same thing `load_agent_runtime()` already does once at startup, [AgentConfiguration.cpp:49-85](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentConfiguration.cpp:49)) and push that into A's already-open bridge — mirroring exactly what Home already does, not a heavier operation.

**Does this fully close the gap I found?** Yes, for the specific staleness scenario: the printer dialog can only be reached from Home or Prepare, so closing it always fires `on_page_changed()` on the way back — meaning A refreshes at exactly the moment it would become visible/relevant again. That's a clean, low-risk fit, not a bolt-on. It also lines up with something I hadn't mentioned: `on_page_changed()` already force-collapses the Agent pane while Home is showing ([ShellController.cpp:507](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.cpp:507)), so there's never a moment where A and B are both visible showing different answers — good, that removes a class of "which one do I believe" confusion.

**Two things this doesn't fix, worth flagging honestly:**
1. It only fixes the availability-staleness problem. The other risk I mentioned last time — both webview instances independently opening the same `mcp.json` discovery file — is untouched by this and would need its own check (I still haven't verified whether `McpRuntime` has any file-locking).
2. Edge case to verify before relying on this: if the user closes the printer dialog *while* the API-key verification is still an in-flight async call (before `commit()` actually finishes), `on_page_changed()` would fire and refresh A too early — and whatever happens to B's pending callback when B gets destroyed mid-flight is a separate lifecycle question I haven't checked.

# Embed Agent Setup inside the Add a Printer dialog

## Context

Today, clicking "Set up the agent" inside the native "Add a printer" dialog
(`PrinterSetupDialog`) closes that modal and redirects the user to the main
Home/Prepare window's docked Agent panel to configure their AI agent —
breaking the flow this dialog exists to keep contained. We're replacing that
redirect with a second, independent `AgentWebView` instance embedded directly
in the dialog, reusing the exact same React setup screens (`SetupChooser`)
rather than rebuilding them natively. That "second instance" choice is
simpler to write than reparenting the app's single docked webview, but it
introduces one real risk we already traced through the code: the docked
panel (webview A) has no way to learn that the embedded one (webview B) just
wrote a working agent config, and will keep showing "No agent connected"
until the app restarts. This plan embeds webview B and closes that staleness
gap using a pattern (`ShellController::on_page_changed()`) that already
exists in this codebase for an analogous problem (the Home gallery).

## Approach

**1. Expose workspace/persistence from `ShellController`.**
`AgentWebView`'s constructor needs `Workspace::IWorkspace&` and
`Agent::ProjectPersistence&` (`AgentWebView.hpp:28-34`), both currently
private to `ShellController` (built at `ShellController.cpp:192,199`) with
no accessor. Add `workspace()`/`persistence()` getters to `ShellController`,
mirroring the existing `agent_pane()` accessor.

**2. Give `PrinterSetupLauncher` a factory for a second `AgentWebView`.**
In `PrinterSetupLauncher.cpp` (which already holds `shell` and constructs the
dialog around lines 63-96), build a
`std::function<std::unique_ptr<Agent::AgentWebView>(wxWindow*)>` that, on
each call, runs `Agent::load_agent_runtime(wxGetApp().app_config)`
(`AgentConfiguration.cpp:49-85` — the same call `ShellController.cpp:201`
makes at shell install) to get a fresh, independent `AgentServicePtr` +
`AgentSetupServicePtr` + starting availability, then constructs
`AgentWebView(parent, theme, shell->workspace(), shell->persistence(),
availability, std::move(service), setup)`. Pass this factory into the
dialog alongside what it already receives.

**Deliberately skip MCP wiring for webview B.** `AgentWebView`'s own
constructor doesn't start MCP — that only happens in the `AgentPane` wrapper
(`AgentPane.cpp:32-67`, `host().start_mcp(discovery_path)`), which we are not
using here. Constructing `AgentWebView` directly (not via `AgentPane`) means
webview B never touches `data_dir()/jusprin/mcp.json` or the preferred MCP
port, sidestepping the discovery-file/port collision that a naive two-`AgentPane`
approach would risk. No extra code needed — this falls out of the
construction choice.

**3. New dialog state hosting the embedded webview.**
`PrinterSetupDialog::set_up_agent()` (`PrinterSetupDialog.cpp:771-775`)
currently does `EndModal(wxID_CANCEL)` + an external `open()` callback.
Change it to: lazily build `m_setup_webview` via the factory (once), call
`m_setup_webview->host().request_setup()` (mirrors
`AgentHost.cpp:1927-1934`, the exact call `ShellController::open_agent_setup()`
already makes at `ShellController.cpp:392-398`) so it opens straight to
`SetupChooser`, set `m_showing_agent_setup = true`, and call `rebuild()`.

In `rebuild()` (`PrinterSetupDialog.cpp:190-230`), branch before the existing
`switch (m_controller->state())`: if `m_showing_agent_setup`, reparent
`m_setup_webview` into the content sizer instead of calling any `build_*()`.

**Reparenting detail that matters:** `rebuild()` calls `m_root->Clear(true)`,
which destroys children — including `m_setup_webview` if it were parented
under `m_root`. `rebuild()` also runs on DPI changes (`on_dpi_changed`,
line 132), not just flow-state changes. Keep `m_setup_webview` parented
directly to the dialog (`this`), and only `Reparent()`/`Show()` it into the
content sizer during `rebuild()` — this way a DPI-triggered rebuild of the
surrounding chrome can't destroy an in-progress setup session (e.g. a
half-typed API key).

**4. Auto-return to the printer flow once setup succeeds.**
Per your answer: once webview B's agent becomes Ready, the dialog should
swap back into the normal flow, not require an extra click or close outright.
`AgentHost` doesn't currently expose an "availability changed" observer —
only outbound calls (`set_agent()`, `set_availability()`). Add a small
completion callback (`std::function<void()>`, invoked once from the same
success path `AgentConfiguration.cpp:110-121`'s `commit()` lambda reaches
via `pump_setup()`, `AgentHost.cpp:1466-1474`) that `PrinterSetupDialog`
subscribes to when constructing webview B. On firing: set
`m_showing_agent_setup = false`, `m_agent_connected = true`, drive
`m_controller` to `FlowState::Initial`, and call `rebuild()` — this lands on
the exact existing branch `if (m_agent_connected) { build_initial(...) }`
already in the switch. Destroy `m_setup_webview` at this point rather than
keeping it alive — it's one-shot and throwaway by design (see point 2).

**5. Fix the docked panel's staleness — `ShellController::on_page_changed()`.**
This is the same hook already used for the Home gallery's "refresh on
return" (`ShellController.cpp:491-508`: `if (home) m_home->refresh();`,
which is `HomeWebView::refresh()` → `push_state()`, `HomeWebView.cpp:94` — a
bridge push, not a full page reload). Extend it: when the completion
callback in step 4 fires, set a small flag on `ShellController` (e.g.
`m_agent_config_possibly_changed = true`) instead of touching webview A
directly (the dialog and the shell are separate objects; this keeps the
coupling one-directional and cheap). In `on_page_changed()`, if that flag is
set, clear it and re-derive availability via `Agent::load_agent_runtime()`
again, then call `m_agent_pane->web_view().host().set_agent(std::move(runtime.service),
runtime.availability)` (`AgentHost.hpp:70`) on webview A. `set_agent()`
already guards on `agent_busy()` (no-ops if A is mid-turn), which is a free
safety net. The flag guard means this only does work right after the
embedded setup actually changed something — not on every ordinary Home↔Prepare
tab flip.

## Files to change

- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.hpp/.cpp` — `workspace()`/
  `persistence()` accessors; the `m_agent_config_possibly_changed` flag +
  setter; extend `on_page_changed()`.
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterSetupLauncher.cpp/.hpp` — build
  the `AgentWebView` factory lambda; pass it (and a way to signal
  `ShellController`'s flag) into the dialog.
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterSetupDialog.hpp/.cpp` — new
  `m_setup_webview`/`m_showing_agent_setup` members; rewritten
  `set_up_agent()`; new `rebuild()` branch; completion-callback handling.
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentHost.hpp/.cpp` — add the small
  "became ready" completion callback alongside the existing `commit()`/
  `set_agent()` success path.

## Reuse (already in the codebase, not new)

- `Agent::load_agent_runtime(AppConfig*)` — `AgentConfiguration.cpp:49-85`.
- `Agent::make_agent_setup(AppConfig*)` — `AgentConfiguration.hpp:42`.
- `AgentHost::request_setup()` — `AgentHost.cpp:1927-1934`.
- `AgentHost::set_agent(AgentServicePtr, AgentAvailability)` —
  `AgentHost.hpp:70`, already guards on `agent_busy()`.
- `HomeWebView::refresh()`/`push_state()` pattern — `HomeWebView.cpp:94` —
  the precedent the whole refresh-on-page-change design mirrors.
- `WipeTowerDialog` (`src/slic3r/GUI/WipeTowerDialog.cpp:366-422`) —
  precedent for hosting a `wxWebView` inside a modal dialog's own sizer.

## Known gap to resolve during implementation

`AgentHost` has no existing "availability changed" observer hook (step 4's
completion callback). This needs to be added as new, small surface area —
confirm there isn't already an equivalent event/signal elsewhere in
`AgentHost`/`AgentWebView` before adding a parallel one.

## Verification

- Build: `cmake --build <worktree>/build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
  --target OrcaSlicer` (absolute path — see worktree build memory).
- Manual, with a scratch `--datadir` and no `OPENAI_API_KEY` configured
  (lands cleanly on the "No agent connected" state):
  1. Click "Set up the agent" — confirm `SetupChooser` renders inside the
     dialog at its native width, and the dialog does **not** close or
     redirect to Home/Prepare.
  2. Complete "Use your own API key" with a valid key — confirm the dialog
     auto-transitions to the Initial evidence-entry state (no extra click,
     dialog stays open).
  3. Close the dialog, open the docked Agent panel on Home/Prepare — confirm
     it now shows Ready immediately (the staleness bug found in the prior
     investigation), with no app restart needed.
  4. Trigger a DPI change (or resize across a DPI boundary) while the
     embedded setup screen is showing, with unsaved input in it (e.g. a
     partially typed API key) — confirm the webview survives the resulting
     `rebuild()` rather than being destroyed and losing that input.
- `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp --printer-setup` and the `shell_theme`/
  `jusprin_fake_bambu` suites should still build and pass unchanged, since
  `PrinterSetupController`/`FlowState` itself isn't modified.

# Embed Agent Setup inside the Add a Printer dialog

## Context

Today, clicking "Set up the agent" inside the native "Add a printer" dialog
(`PrinterSetupDialog`) closes that modal and redirects the user to the main
Home/Prepare window's docked Agent panel to configure their AI agent —
breaking the flow this dialog exists to keep contained. We're replacing that
redirect with a second, independent `AgentWebView` instance embedded directly
in the dialog, reusing the exact same React setup screens (`SetupChooser`)
rather than rebuilding them natively. That "second instance" choice is
simpler to write than reparenting the app's single docked webview, but it
introduces one real risk we already traced through the code: the docked
panel (webview A) has no way to learn that the embedded one (webview B) just
wrote a working agent config, and will keep showing "No agent connected"
until the app restarts. This plan embeds webview B and closes that staleness
gap using a pattern (`ShellController::on_page_changed()`) that already
exists in this codebase for an analogous problem (the Home gallery).

**1. Expose workspace/persistence from `ShellController`.**
`AgentWebView`'s constructor needs `Workspace::IWorkspace&` and
`Agent::ProjectPersistence&` (`AgentWebView.hpp:28-34`), both currently
private to `ShellController` (built at `ShellController.cpp:192,199`) with
no accessor. Add `workspace()`/`persistence()` getters to `ShellController`,
mirroring the existing `agent_pane()` accessor.

**2. Give `PrinterSetupLauncher` a factory for a second `AgentWebView`.**
In `PrinterSetupLauncher.cpp` (which already holds `shell` and constructs the
dialog around lines 63-96), build a

each call, runs `Agent::load_agent_runtime(wxGetApp().app_config)`
(`AgentConfiguration.cpp:49-85` — the same call `ShellController.cpp:201`
makes at shell install) to get a fresh, independent `AgentServicePtr` +
`AgentSetupServicePtr` + starting availability, then constructs
`AgentWebView(parent, theme, shell->workspace(), shell->persistence(),
availability, std::move(service), setup)`. Pass this factory into the
dialog alongside what it already receives.

**Deliberately skip MCP wiring for webview B.** `AgentWebView`'s own
constructor doesn't start MCP — that only happens in the `AgentPane` wrapper

Implemented the design from [[add-printer-flow-figma-discrepancy]]'s follow-up
discussion: `PrinterSetupDialog`'s "Set up the agent" button no longer closes
the modal and redirects to the docked Agent panel. It now builds a second,
throwaway `AgentWebView` (own `AgentService`/`AgentSetupService`, no
`start_mcp()` call) and embeds it directly in the dialog.

**Key pieces, for the next session touching this:**
- `PrinterSetupDialog::set_up_agent()` lazily builds `m_setup_webview` via an
  injected `MakeSetupWebViewFn` factory, calls `host().request_setup()` to
  open straight to `SetupChooser`, and rebuilds. A completion callback
  (`AgentHost::set_setup_completed_listener`, new — didn't exist before)
  fires once `pump_setup()` successfully installs the verified agent; it sets
  `m_agent_connected = true` and `CallAfter`s the teardown (destroying the
  webview from a callback invoked by that same webview's own host would be
  use-after-free otherwise).
- `rebuild()` must detach `m_setup_webview` from its sizer *before*
  `m_root->Clear(true)` on every call (including DPI-change rebuilds), since
  `Clear(true)` destroys sizer children.
- Docked-panel staleness fix: `ShellController::mark_agent_config_possibly_changed()`
  sets a flag consumed by `on_page_changed()` (the same hook already used for
  `m_home->refresh()`), which re-derives availability via
  `Agent::load_agent_runtime()` and pushes it into the docked pane's
  `AgentHost::set_agent()` — not a full webview reload.
- **Chrome-stripping fix (added after initial implementation, per Kenneth's
  live feedback):** the embedded webview initially showed the full chat page
  shell (ChatHeader "New chat" title, +, ... buttons) around the setup card,
  because it loads the exact same `index.html`/`App.tsx` as the docked panel.
  Fixed with a new `AppProps.embedded` prop (read from `?embedded=1` in the
  page URL, set by `AgentWebView`'s new `embedded` ctor param) that makes
  `App.tsx` early-return just `{errorNotice}` + `body()`, skipping
  ChatHeader/chatList/Composer/external-actions entirely. Requires `npm run
  build` in `AgentUI/` after editing App.tsx/main.tsx — the output goes
  straight to `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html`, which on this worktree's
  build is a **symlink to the source tree** (`Contents/Resources` →
  worktree `resources/`), so a rebuilt bundle is live immediately with no
  CMake step, but the changed .hpp/.cpp signatures still need a C++ rebuild.

**Transient crash during testing, not fully root-caused:** two early manual
test attempts (both on a repeatedly re-signed, repeatedly `pkill`-killed test
`.app` copy, launched via `open`-equivalent `nohup ... &`) crashed silently
right after clicking "Set up the agent" — no crash report, log just stopped
after "finished run wizard". Four subsequent attempts (a completely fresh
app copy on first launch, plus three consecutive retries under `lldb` in one
session) all succeeded cleanly. Working hypothesis, unconfirmed: stale
WebKit/XPC state from abruptly killing and relaunching the same signed
bundle identity repeatedly (matches the `XPC_ERROR_CONNECTION_INVALID
from launchservicesd` / sandbox noise seen under lldb, though that noise
appeared on a successful run too so it may be unrelated benign chatter). If
this resurfaces, try a full `killall` of any stray `com.apple.WebKit.*`
processes before relaunching, or test with `quit` (not `pkill`) between runs.

**Pre-existing, unrelated to this change:** `JusPrinShellHarness
--printer-setup`'s `setup_network_access_code_is_validated` step hangs
indefinitely (confirmed twice, before and after this change, at the exact
same point) — it's reached before `verify_setup_no_agent` (my modified test)
even runs, so not a regression from this work, but the full harness run
could not be used to verify `verify_setup_no_agent` end-to-end this session.
Verified that scenario manually instead (live app, `?embedded=1` confirmed
in the actual rendered dialog).

Related: [[add-printer-flow-figma-discrepancy]], [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]].

`JusPrinShellHarness --printer-setup` hung forever at
`setup_network_access_code_is_validated`, reached before `verify_setup_no_agent`

Root cause, found via `lldb -p <pid> -b -o "breakpoint set -f SetupCommands.cpp -l 369" -o run -o "frame variable error"`:
`SetupCommands.cpp:368`'s `error = _L("Invalid input.")` was live-observed
returning `"Invalid input"` with **no trailing period** — not a `wxStaticText::Wrap()`
rendering artifact (the wxString itself lacked the period at assignment).

→ `msgstr "Invalid input"` (missing punctuation) — an upstream OrcaSlicer
translation-catalog inconsistency (most other languages, e.g. cs/ca/it/fr/es/pl/ru,
do have the period; en/de/hu/nl/ja/sv/th don't), not something JusPrin
introduced. Fixed with a one-line `.po` edit plus `msgfmt --check-format -o
resources/i18n/en/JusPrin2.mo localization/i18n/en/OrcaSlicer_en.po` (matching
CMakeLists.txt:745's exact invocation) — safe to regenerate directly: the
`.mo` is gitignored (`*.mo` in `.gitignore`), a pure local build artifact
never tracked in git, so only the single-line `.po` source change is a real
diff. After the fix, the full `--printer-setup` harness passes clean: 127
checks, 0 failures, including all nine `setup_no_agent_*` checks.

Getting there required fixing a real, pre-existing bug that was blocking the harness before it ever reached my test. `setup_network_access_code_is_validated` was hanging forever waiting for the text "Invalid input." I confirmed with a debugger that the string itself, not just its on-screen rendering, was missing the period the moment it got set, and traced it to a translation file: `localization/i18n/en/OrcaSlicer_en.po` maps `"Invalid input."` to `"Invalid input"` — the period got dropped somewhere upstream in OrcaSlicer's translation catalog (most other languages have it correctly; English and a handful of others don't). Not something this session's work caused, but it was silently breaking this specific automated test path.

I fixed the one-line `.po` entry and regenerated the compiled catalog. That `.mo` file is git-ignored — a local build artifact, never checked into version control — so the only real change is the single-line translation fix, which is about as minimal and safe as a fix gets.

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Embed Agent Setup inside the Add a printer dialog

"Set up the agent" used to close the printer-setup modal and redirect
to the docked Agent panel on Home/Prepare, breaking the flow the dialog
exists to keep contained. It now embeds a second, throwaway AgentWebView
directly in the dialog, with its own independent agent/setup service and
no MCP wiring, reusing the exact same setup screens instead of rebuilding
them natively.

The React page gained an `embedded` mode (loaded via ?embedded=1) that
renders only the setup sub-component, without the docked panel's chat
header, conversation list, or composer around it.

Since the docked panel has no way to learn that the embedded instance
just configured a working agent, ShellController now refreshes the
docked panel's availability when the person returns to Home/Prepare
(mirroring the existing pattern already used to refresh Home's gallery
on return), instead of it staying stuck on "no agent" until restart.
EOF
)"
